extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and USPTO decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: A formal USPTO Final Order resolving a disciplinary complaint by means of a settlement agreement; describes jurisdiction, stipulated facts, legal conclusions, sanctions, reporting requirements, and procedural steps for enforcement. Targets conduct and remedial measures for a registered patent attorney who submitted checks returned for insufficient funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve settlement (jurisdiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter and the authority to approve the proposed settlement agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary complaints must be submitted for approval to the USPTO Director (or designee) and are governed by the cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement ... satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, [and] resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed settlement should set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and must meet the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.26 to be approved and to resolve related disciplinary claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct: submitting checks returned for insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(6) by submitting checks that were returned for insufficient funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting checks or electronic fund transfers to the USPTO that are returned for insufficient funds constitutes a violation of the USPTO Disciplinary Rules and may support disciplinary sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction type: stayed suspension plus probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a period of 24 months ... and the suspension is immediately stayed ... Respondent serve[s] a 24-month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions may include a suspension that is stayed conditioned on probation; the stay can be lifted for noncompliance, resulting in active suspension up to the stayed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain client funds in a client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must maintain funds he receives from his clients for patent law services to be rendered in a client trust account and not in a business/operating account or personal account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating client funds from business funds is required; failure to maintain client funds in a trust account is a compliance metric subject to monitoring and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to avoid issuing checks that are subsequently returned for insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not issue checks from the client trust account or business/operating account that are subsequently returned to the Office because they were drawn on insufficient funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A condition of probation and continued practice is that payments to the Office clear; any returned checks are a specific trigger for enforcement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent CPA review and periodic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, at his own expense, hire a certified public accountant to review Respondent's legal practice and to prepare and submit a report to the OED Director at six months, 12 months, 18 months, and 24 months after the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each CPA report must indicate whether Respondent is maintaining client funds in a trust account and not issuing checks that are later returned, and must specifically identify each transaction where Respondent failed to maintain client funds or issued a returned check. Deadlines may be extended only by written agreement of the Respondent and the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted practice during probation unless stay lifted
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is permitted to practice patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO during his probationary period unless the stay of the suspension is lifted by order of the USPTO Director or his designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed practice during probation depends on the stay remaining in effect; lifting the stay removes privilege to practice and triggers suspension consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause ... send the Order to Respondent at the last address of record ... and grant Respondent 15 days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance initiates a specific procedural sequence: issuance and service of an Order to Show Cause with a 15-day response period, providing Respondent an opportunity to respond before further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director to lift stay and impose suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If after the 15-day period the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause; (ii) Respondent's response, if any; and (iii) evidence ... and request that the USPTO Director immediately lift the stay of the suspension and suspend Respondent for up to 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director compiles the record and may request the USPTO Director to lift the stay and impose the previously stayed suspension based on the evidence of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs the OED Director to publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room ... and to publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette. The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions and notices are to be publicly disseminated via the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette as required by regulation; some dissemination rules (§§ 11.58 and 11.60) may not apply unless the stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if suspension is imposed (access and credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended: (1) Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; (4) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated; (5) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active suspension results in loss of access to USPTO electronic credentials and customer numbers until reinstatement; dissemination and compliance obligations follow regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review on immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that the USPTO Director or his designee lifts the stay of the suspension and Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's decision to lift the stay, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension of Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing for review does not stay the immediate effect of a lifted stay; suspension goes into effect notwithstanding a pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, be considered: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct ... and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary outcomes may be used as aggravation or rebuttal in later complaints or proceedings concerning similar conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms can specify that each party bears its own costs rather than imposing monetary costs or restitution beyond specified sanctions and remedial steps.
